payload.rationale: The resolution depends on the September 2026 seasonally adjusted CPI-U rounding to 0.3% or higher (an unrounded increase of at least 0.25%). EIA weekly gasoline prices show a significant increase in the first half of September, rising from $4.207 on August 31 to $4.455 on September 14. With gasoline comprising roughly 3.77% of the CPI basket, a ~6% increase in gasoline prices would alone contribute over 0.2% to the headline CPI. Given that core CPI has recently been running around 0.2% to 0.3% (August core rose 0.3%), the combination of steady core inflation and a positive energy contribution makes a headline print of 0.3% or higher highly probable.
limitations: Gasoline prices for the second half of September are not yet known and could reverse.
Seasonal adjustment factors for energy and other components can introduce volatility and differ from unadjusted retail price trends.
Other volatile components like food or core goods could surprise to the downside, offsetting the energy increase.
